ca_inner_gorge.blurb: Inner Gorge is one section of the Owens River Gorge, a volcanic canyon on the Eastern Sierra side of Bishop. The rock is tuff, with edges, pockets and cracks. Nearly everything is bolted sport, with only a thin scattering of trad. Grades centre on 5.10 through 5.12, with a fair handful of moderates below that and only a few climbs at 5.13 and up. The northern end is narrower and tends to be quieter, while the southern end turns steeper and harder around Dilithium Crystal and Eldorado Roof. Supreme Wizard Formation and Mothership Cliff are other big concentrations of routes. The gorge as a whole is treated as a year-round crag, though summer heat can be a problem.

qc_val_david_bouldering.blurb: Val David Bouldering lies in the Laurentians of Quebec, within the regional park shared by Val-David and Val-Morin. The rock is Laurentian granite, and the climbing is technical in character, with moves that some compare to Squamish. Nearly all of it is bouldering, with a smaller number of trad lines and very few sport routes. Grades begin at V0 and climb steadily, with plenty of problems between V2 and V7 and a thinner tail of hard ones at the top end. Les Dames and Les Hommes hold most of the problems, and the Les Hommes boulders are generally unintimidating, so a solo session is realistic. The area is usually not crowded and the walk in is short.

az_sycamore_canyon.blurb: Sycamore Canyon is a big drainage on the Mogollon Rim in northern Arizona, set in thick ponderosa pine forest within reach of Flagstaff. The walls are columnar basalt, and the climbing is overwhelmingly trad, much of it steep hand and fist cracks, with only a handful of sport lines. Grades run from 5.7 up past 5.13, but the bulk sits between 5.10 and 5.12, and ratings are known to be stout. Paradise Forks is the most developed crag, with routes mostly reached by rappelling in from above. Volunteer Canyon feels bigger and wilder, with longer, steeper lines and rappels to specific belays. Whitetail Canyon is a newer, smaller addition.

me_clifton_crags.blurb: Clifton Crags is a cluster of crags in rolling hills about twenty minutes east of Bangor, Maine. Roped climbing is the main draw, split fairly evenly between sport and trad, with some top-rope and a good number of boulder problems too. Most routes are one to three pitches, and grades mostly fall between 5.7 and 5.11, with a handful of 5.12s and easier outings below. Eagle Bluff is the best known and largest, with sport and trad routes plus boulders. Parks Pond Bluff is mainly slab with some vertical walls and sunset views over the pond. Big Chick Hill is also slab climbing and suits both newer and experienced leaders.

ut_river_road.blurb: River Road follows the Colorado River northeast of Moab, with climbing scattered along most of the stretch toward Dewey Bridge. It is a large, spread-out area and the style is very mixed: bouldering is the biggest share, with trad and sport close behind and a couple of aid lines. The sandstone is fragile. Big Bend Bouldering Area is one of Moab's most popular boulder spots, on Wingate sandstone, with problems from V0 into the hard grades and best conditions from October through March. Take-Out Beach is the largest sport crag, while River Road Dihedrals and Northside Routes hold trad. Roped grades mostly run 5.9 to 5.11, with a few 5.12s.

va_old_rag.blurb: Old Rag is a granite mountain inside Shenandoah National Park in Virginia, better known to hikers than to climbers. The rock is old and solid, with splitters, corners and faces, and the climbing is mainly traditional, with bolts few and far between, so a full rack is the norm. Most routes are a single pitch, and a smaller set of boulder problems and sport routes sits alongside them. Grades run from easy to 5.12, with the weight on 5.8 through 5.11. The crags are scattered across the mountain, including Reflector Oven, Skyline Wall and Lower God's Area. Spring and fall are generally recommended, since summer brings heat, black flies and nettles, while winter can be cold but sunny.
